newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philipine army, rebels sign ceasefire accord.
newsitem.headline: Philipine army, rebels sign ceasefire accord.

text.p: The Philippine army and Moslem guerrillas signed an interim ceasefire agreement on Monday, halting fighting in a nearby town that has killed at least 33 guerrillas and four soldiers, the military said.
The fighting also has forced at least 2,000 villagers to flee their homes in Buldon town, Maguindanao province, where clashes first began two weeks ago and continued sporadicaly until last weekend.
The ceasefire accord was signed by Army Major-General Joselin Nazareno and Lannang Ali, a lawyer for the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), which is fighting for an Islamic state.

The pact requires both sides to refrain from provocative actions such as deploying forces outside areas they now control, and bars the MILF from setting up checkpoints on roads leading to Buldon, rebels and army officials said.
The MILF is a breakaway faction of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), which signed a peace accord with Manila last September ending its 24-year revolt for autonomy.
The government and the MILF have held preliminary talks on a separate peace deal and a permanent ceasefire covering other areas besides Buldon, and are to meet again next month.
